messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: infra-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Dry-run] Private fleet patch dry‑run: preflight sim results & rollback play

Team,

Thanks for joining the dry‑run this morning. Attached are the raw preflight sim outputs we ran against AcmeHealth's VPC fleet (preflight-sim-summary.csv) and an early rollback playbook (rollback-playbook-v2.md).

High‑level: the simulation exercised a staged pin/unpin on a 3‑shard subset (shards a/c/e). We validated: BGP route retention, MTU/PMTU checks across the transit (10.2.0.0/16) path, and KV cache warmup behavior when switching from model v3.1.2 -> v3.2.0. Noted items below that need engineering triage before the scheduled maintenance window.

Immediate asks (owners and ETA):
- Karthik: confirm NIC driver offload compatibility on the bonded interfaces; see nic-compat-matrix.xlsx (ETA EOD 6/26).
- Laura: update the canary cohort mapping so shard 'e' is the fall‑back cohort if a hotfail occurs (ETA 6/27).
- Soojin: add a step to the preflight that proactively rotates the control‑plane certs 24h before the window (ETA PR to the playbook by 6/26).

Acme ops: Samantha — thanks for the test SSH access and topology snapshot. Can you confirm whether your upstream transit has any active route‑filters that might strip BGP community tags? That affects our canary promotion logic.

Attachments: preflight-sim-summary.csv, rollback-playbook-v2.md, nic-compat-matrix.xlsx

Next sync: 4pm PT to review updated playbook and sign off on comms.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Dry-run] Private fleet patch dry‑run: preflight sim results & rollback play

Vanessa — thanks, quick notes from the runtime/serving side after reviewing the sim CSV: 

1) NIC/drivers: our sim showed degraded perf with SR‑IOV disabled on node class c (p99 token latency doubled). Possible cause: fallback to software path for GIC offload. I'll run the vendor kernel module tests against node images and populate nic-compat-matrix.xlsx with exact kernel+driver combinations that pass. If we can't get SR‑IOV reliably, we need to widen canary window.

2) KV cache warmup: when we pinned v3.2.0 for shard 'a', warmup stalled for <4 minutes due to parallel init requests. Mitigation: staggered cache priming (we should prewarm via background sync to a cold replica before weight flip). I'll add a script and an init lock to the playbook.

3) Route tags & promotion: the canary logic currently relies on community tag 0x0af1 to identify promoted prefixes. If Acme transit strips that, our automated promotion will never fire. Samantha — if tags are removed, we will need a manual opt‑in step (human‑confirmed promotion) or a fallback TTL‑based promotion after 10 minutes.

I'll push a branch with the SR‑IOV tests and the cache prewarm script by EOD.

-Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Thanks Vanessa & Karthik — appreciate the notes. A few points from Acme infra: 

- We do have a transit ACL that strips most BGP community tags on egress to partner clouds. We can whitelist community 0x0af1 for the maintenance window but need a signed change request. Can we include the CR in the rollback-playbook-v2.md as a pre‑window dependency?
- We will not be available to rotate CA certs during the maintenance itself; rotation must happen 24h prior (Soojin's suggestion aligns).
- We'll provide a scoped runbook for our network team (will upload to the Drive link you provided).

Proposed customer sign‑off timeline: get final playbook by 6/27 EOD, small tabletop on 6/28 at 10am ET, maintenance window 6/29 00:00–04:00 ET. Does Redwood need any additional preflight access tokens or an updated jump host?

Samantha
Senior Cloud Engineer — AcmeHealth

All — good progress. Final summary and owners below (I'll update the Drive doc as the single source of truth):

1) SR‑IOV / NIC compatibility — owner: Karthik Iyer — deliverable: nic-compat-matrix.xlsx updated with pass/fail + remediation steps. Blocker gating roll: YES if >10% of canary nodes fail. (ETA 6/26 EOD)
2) Cache prewarm script & init lock — owner: Karthik Iyer — deliverable: PR with script + test results. Rollback effect: safe (idempotent). (ETA 6/26 EOD)
3) Canary cohort change (make shard 'e' failover lane) — owner: Laura Bennett — deliverable: updated canary mapping + ops checklist. (ETA 6/27)
4) Cert rotation prewindow — owner: Soojin Lee — deliverable: playbook step & confirmation that Acme rotates 24h before window. (ETA 6/26)
5) Transit community whitelist CR — owner: Acme (Samantha) — deliverable: CR link in Drive before 6/28 tabletop.

Decision points: if the NIC matrix shows SR‑IOV regressions, we widen canary window to 45m and run an additional validation cohort. If route tags are not available, promotion will be manual with a 10m TTL fallback.

Next steps: 4pm PT sync cancelled (we'll triage asynchronously). Please update the Drive doc and ping here when your deliverable is uploaded.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Head of Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
